text:
maya: Quick q — trying to capture a very short (1.5-2s) hotspot during batching + KV-prefetch. nsys keeps either grabbing huge files or missing the OSRT markers entirely. Anyone do a sane short-burst capture that reliably includes NVTX/osrt ranges?
ben: We do this a lot for the new kernel selector regressions. Two tips: 1) bracket the exact GPU work with NVTX and use capture-range, 2) use sampling mode + very short duration to avoid huge files.
ivan: Example command we use:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=2000ms -o shortburst -- your_binary --args
```
That gets a small file but you still need NVTX ranges around the KV lookup + batch boundary.
sam: If OSRT markers are missing, check that the runtime is emitting them on the GPU thread (not only host). We had a bug where osrt ranges were emitted from the wrong thread id and nsys ignored them.
maya: ah that explains a past miss — we put NVTX_PUSH on the batching thread but the kernel launch happens on a worker thread. Is there a quick check?
ben: Two quick checks: (1) run with `--trace=nvtx` only and open in the GUI, see if ranges line up with cuda kernels. (2) dump nvtx via env var in debug build to stdout (we have a tiny helper that echoes NVTX pushes with thread id).
perf-bot: FYI estimate: a 2s capture with trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt + sample=cpu usually ~15-30MB depending on kernel churn. If you're seeing >200MB you likely captured continuous GPU timeline.
ivan: Another approach is capture-range by pid/tid to bracket the exact frames: `--capture-range=cpu:tid:100-120` (our wrapper translates to correct nsys syntax). That avoids the long warmup noise.
sam: Also important: warmup off the trace. Start your app, run ~5-10 short inferences to populate KV cache and kernels, then trigger capture-range for the single critical request. Otherwise KV-evict/warmup noise blurs the hotspot.
maya: Good call. We were launching capture at process start which recorded warmup eviction spikes. I'll switch to bracketed capture and NVTX around the lookup + kernel.
ben: If you need to correlate kernel name -> batch size: add nvtx payload like `nvtxRangePushA("batch_size=8,kv_hit=1")` before the request. Then in the timeline you can filter NVTX text.
maya: One last gotcha we hit: nsys sampling can miss very short kernels (<50us). For that we use full trace for cuda but combine with capture-range to keep file size bounded: `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=3s` and trigger exactly around the target window.
ivan: TL;DR: warmup first, emit NVTX on the launching thread, use capture-range to bracket, prefer sample=cpu for quick sanity runs and full cuda trace for microkernel hunting.
maya: Thanks — doing warmup + bracketed osrt + small nvtx payloads now. Will post the capture if it still looks off. :thumbsup:
